title: Replacement System Installations Refund Standards: Returning Money to the Lender and the Homeowner
content:
# Refunds on installation projects

## The project balance

The project balance of a Replacement System Installations project is the amount the homeowner owes on the project. Charges and refunds raise it; credits and payments, including lender funding, lower it. A negative project balance is money Harbison owes the homeowner.

## Refund standards

1. A refund is owed whenever the project balance is negative after cancellation credits, other credits and fees.
2. The lender's financing disbursement is returned first, to the financing account it came from, up to the amount disbursed, so that a financed homeowner's loan balance falls before any money is returned to the homeowner.
3. Any remainder is returned to the homeowner's own payments in reverse order of posting, each refund to the method of the payment it names and never more than that payment.
4. A refund returned to the financing account reduces the loan as a merchant refund credit on that account.
5. A refund is posted only for a payment that exists on the project.
6. A warranty unit replacement credit from a protection contract claim reduces a replacement project's balance like any other credit and is never refunded in cash.

Payments received are counted over the project's life to the date of handling, net of refunds already returning them, kept separately for lender disbursements and for all other payments.

## Worked example (hypothetical project)

A hypothetical project shows a balance of −$3000.00 after cancellation credits. Its payments are a $2000.00 lender disbursement, a $1500.00 card deposit posted first and an $800.00 bank-transfer progress payment posted later.

| Order | Payment returned | Refund |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Lender disbursement, to the financing account | $2000.00 |
| 2 | Progress payment (latest homeowner payment), by bank transfer | $800.00 |
| 3 | Deposit, to the card | $200.00 |

The $2000.00 returned to the financing account reduces the loan as a merchant refund credit; the three refunds total $3000.00.
